title: Entrywise matrix equality to find trace
trigger: When a matrix is given by two different entrywise expressions and said to be equal, match corresponding entries to solve for the unknowns, then sum the resulting diagonal entries to get the trace.

title: Outer product dimension of column times row vector
trigger: For nonzero vectors x, y in R^n written as column vectors, x*y^T multiplies an (n x 1) matrix by a (1 x n) matrix, so use the dimension rule (n x 1)(1 x n) = n x n to get the shape directly, without expanding entries.

title: Matrix product rows/columns as linear combinations
trigger: Row i of AB equals (row i of A) times B, i.e. a linear combination of the rows of B weighted by row i of A; likewise column j of AB is A times column j of B, a linear combination of columns of A. Check each answer option against this row/column rule rather than multiplying out full matrices.

title: Existence of nilpotent vs symmetric matrices
trigger: Recall that a real symmetric matrix is always diagonalizable with real eigenvalues, so symmetric + nilpotent (A^2=0) forces all eigenvalues to be 0 and hence A=0; but a non-symmetric nilpotent nonzero matrix always exists (e.g. [[0,1],[0,0]]). Test each assertion/statement against these two facts.

title: Determinant of a 3x3 matrix via cofactor expansion
trigger: Expand along a row (usually the one with the most zeros) using signed cofactors: det = a11*M11 - a12*M12 + a13*M13 (checkerboard sign pattern), computing each 2x2 minor by cross-multiplying.

title: Dot product equals zero to solve for an unknown or test orthogonality
trigger: Translate each object (vector, or line ax+by=0 whose direction/normal vector is (a,b) or (b,-a)) into a vector, set the dot product of the two vectors to zero, and solve the resulting linear equation for the unknown component or ratio.

title: Angle between two lines via the dot-product cosine formula
trigger: Write the direction vectors of both lines, apply cos(theta) = |v1.v2| / (|v1||v2|) to get the acute angle, then compute the requested trig expression (e.g. 1/cos^2(theta)) from that cosine value.

title: Determinant scaling under row/column operations
trigger: When a row or column is scaled by c, det multiplies by c; swapping two rows flips the sign of det; adding a multiple of one row to another leaves det unchanged — chain these rules to compute the new determinant or to test/identify which operation sequence produces a target value.

title: Recover det(A) from row-reduction-to-identity steps
trigger: List each elementary row operation used to reduce A to I, multiply together the scale factors (and a -1 per row swap) that those operations applied to the determinant so that the product times det(A) equals det(I)=1, then solve backward for det(A).

title: Determinant of a matrix polynomial via factoring
trigger: Factor the matrix polynomial expression into a product of simpler matrix factors (e.g. A^6-A^5 = A^5(A-I), A^3-3A^2+2A = A(A-I)(A-2I)), then use det(XY)=det(X)det(Y) and det(cA)=c^n det(A) so the whole thing reduces to a product of easily-computed determinants (often forcing a 0 factor).

title: Set det(A)=0 to find parameter for nontrivial/infinite solutions
trigger: A homogeneous system Ax=0 (or an invertibility requirement) has nontrivial/infinitely many solutions exactly when det(A)=0; expand det(A) symbolically in the unknown parameter(s) and solve that equation, or require det(A)≠0 for the only-trivial/unique-solution case.

title: Consistency of Ax=b via Gaussian elimination / augmented-matrix rank
trigger: Row reduce the augmented matrix [A|b] down to echelon form; the system is consistent iff rank(A) = rank([A|b]), so read off the condition on b's entries (or on a parameter) that makes the final pivot-free row read 0 = 0 rather than 0 = nonzero.

title: Solve for an unknown component via Cramer's rule
trigger: For a square system Ax=b with det(A)≠0, compute x_i = det(A_i)/det(A), where A_i is A with column i replaced by b — use this to pull out just the needed component(s) instead of doing full elimination.

title: True/false theory check on rank, invertibility, and solution space
trigger: Test each candidate statement against the core equivalences (A invertible ⇔ det(A)≠0 ⇔ rank(A)=n ⇔ Ax=0 has only the trivial solution) to eliminate false options, and use rank/pivot counting to identify the geometric solution set (point, line, plane, or empty) of an intersecting-planes system.

title: Subspace test via closure + zero vector
trigger: To decide if a set is a (sub)space, check it contains the zero vector and is closed under vector addition and scalar multiplication; failing any single axiom disqualifies the whole set.

title: Column space / span as a plane or line equation
trigger: Write the span (or column space) as the set of all linear combinations of the given vectors, row-reduce to extract the constraint equation it satisfies (e.g. a plane ax+by+cz=0), then match candidate descriptions against that equation, intersecting with any second subspace if asked.

title: Ax=b solvability via column space and rank
trigger: Ax=b has a solution iff b lies in the column space of A, i.e. rank(A) = rank([A|b]); use this rank comparison to judge statements about existence, uniqueness, and independence of the columns.

title: Automatic dependence by dimension count
trigger: If the number of vectors exceeds the dimension of the ambient space (e.g. 4 vectors in R^3), the set is automatically linearly dependent -- no row reduction or determinant needed.

title: Determinant/rank test for dependence with a parameter
trigger: Stack the vectors as rows (or columns) of a square matrix and set its determinant to zero (or reduce and find when a pivot vanishes / rank drops) to solve for the parameter values that make the set dependent or fail to span the whole space.

title: Span membership: solve for parameter then combination coefficients
trigger: To test if v3 lies in span{v1,v2}, set v3 = a*v1 + b*v2 componentwise, solve the resulting linear system first for any unknown entry of v3 and then for the coefficients a,b (may be asked as separate follow-on parts).

title: Unique combination implies basis, dim = count
trigger: If every vector in V can be written uniquely as a linear combination of v1,...,vn, then {v1,...,vn} is automatically a basis (uniqueness forces both independence and spanning), so dim(V) equals n.

title: Dimension/basis of subspace defined by linear equations
trigger: Rewrite the defining equations as a homogeneous linear system, solve for the free variables to parametrize the general solution; dim = number of free variables, and the vectors obtained by setting one free variable to 1 (others 0) form a basis, so check any candidate basis set against this count and against satisfying the equations.

title: Dimension of a span via rank of vectors
trigger: Stack the given vectors as rows (or columns) of a matrix and row-reduce; dim(span) equals the number of nonzero rows (rank) after elimination, and any vector that reduces to zero (a combination of the others) does not add to the count.

title: Dimension of abstract/matrix vector spaces via explicit basis
trigger: Write a general element of the space using free parameters (e.g., free matrix entries subject to the given constraints, or free coefficients), split it into a sum of parameter-times-fixed-vector terms, and count the number of independent parameters — that count is the dimension and the fixed vectors form a basis.

title: Extending a linearly independent set to a basis
trigger: Use the extension theorem: any linearly independent set in a finite-dimensional V can be extended to a basis of V, so its size is at most dim(V), and if its size already equals dim(V) it is already a basis.

title: Isomorphism of finite-dim vector spaces via equal dimension
trigger: Two finite-dimensional vector spaces are isomorphic iff they have the same dimension, so compute dim(W) first, then compute (or bound) the dimension of each candidate space/subspace and match it against dim(W).

title: Kernel/solution-space dimension via solving homogeneous system
trigger: Write the defining condition(s) as Av=0, row-reduce to find rank(A), then dim(kernel)=n-rank(A); apply rank-nullity in reverse to get rank once nullity is known.

title: Injective/surjective decided by comparing domain and codomain dimensions
trigger: For T:R^n->R^m, use rank(A)<=min(m,n): if n>m, T can never be injective (kernel is forced nontrivial); if n<m, T can never be surjective; decide directly from the shape/dimensions without building the matrix.

title: Invertible or isomorphic map forces zero nullity
trigger: If a matrix/map is given (or shown) to be invertible, an isomorphism, or orthogonal, its nullspace is {0} and nullity=0 immediately -- no row reduction needed.

title: Reconstruct T from its action on a basis
trigger: Write the target input vector as a linear combination of the given basis vectors (solve for the scalars), then apply T linearly to their known images to build T(v); the same idea run in reverse lets you pick an unspecified image so T becomes invertible.

title: Ax=b consistency, column space, and uniqueness statement-checking
trigger: Ax=b is consistent iff b lies in Col(A) iff rank(A)=rank([A|b]); the solution (when it exists) is unique iff ker(A)={0}, i.e. rank(A)=n -- test each answer statement against these two facts.

title: Bounding rank or nullity from map dimensions alone
trigger: Use rank(A)<=min(rows,cols) together with rank-nullity (nullity=n-rank) to find the extreme possible rank or nullity without an explicit matrix; when A^2=0, also use Im(A) subset Ker(A) to tighten the bound.

title: Composed maps and multi-statement isomorphism reasoning
trigger: Track how rank, nullity, and injectivity/surjectivity propagate through composition (S∘T, T∘S) or between a map and a related subspace, rather than computing one fixed matrix -- check each statement against rank-nullity applied at each stage.

title: Matrix representation via T(e_i) in standard basis
trigger: To find the standard matrix of T, apply T to each standard basis vector e_i and write the results as columns; in reverse, read the columns of a given standard matrix as T(e_i) and combine them to recover T's formula.

title: Matrix representation in one non-standard ordered basis
trigger: Apply T to each vector of the given ordered basis B, express each image as a linear combination of B's own basis vectors (not the standard basis), and use those coordinates as the columns of [T]_B.

title: General [T] w.r.t. two different bases B1 (domain), B2 (codomain)
trigger: Apply T to each vector of the domain basis B1, then express each image in coordinates of the codomain basis B2 (solve the linear combination) -- those coordinate vectors form the columns of [T]_{B2,B1}; to go backward, multiply [T]_{B2,B1} by a B1-coordinate vector and convert back to standard form (matrix of T-inverse is just the inverse of this matrix), and remember that any invertible square matrix can represent the identity map for a suitably chosen basis pair.

title: Rank and nullity by directly solving T(v)=0
trigger: Set T(x,y,z)=0 and solve the resulting linear system to get a basis for the kernel (nullity = its dimension), then use rank = n - nullity (or find a basis for the range directly) to answer rank questions -- for an isomorphism the matrix is automatically full rank.

title: Rank-nullity theorem to judge kernel/range/injectivity claims
trigger: Compute rank and nullity of the transformation's matrix, then use rank-nullity (dim domain = rank + nullity) together with the definitions -- injective iff nullity=0, surjective iff rank=dim codomain, kernel/range bases from RREF -- to evaluate each statement or combine the dimensions (e.g. m+n+r) asked for.

title: Matrix power structure: nilpotent index / null space of A^2
trigger: Identify the operator's structural type from its definition (nilpotent: A^k=0 for some k, or idempotent/projection: A^2=A), then reason with that algebraic identity directly on basis vectors -- rather than full matrix multiplication -- to find the smallest k with A^k=0 or the null space of A^2.

title: Rank of a matrix via row reduction to echelon form
trigger: Row-reduce the matrix to echelon form and count nonzero rows (or spot a rank-1 structure like x*y^T where every row/column is a scalar multiple of one vector).

title: Rank of a matrix with an unknown parameter - case split
trigger: Row-reduce keeping the parameter symbolic; the rank drops exactly when a pivot expression in the parameter vanishes, so solve that expression = 0 to find the critical value(s).

title: Affine subspace as point-plus-subspace: find U and its dimension
trigger: Write the affine subspace as {p + u : u in U} by picking any point p on it, then homogenize (set the constant/offset term to 0) to get the defining equations of the direction subspace U; dim(U) = n - rank of that homogeneous system.

title: Dimension and intersection of affine solution sets
trigger: The solution set of Ax=b (when consistent) is an affine subspace of dimension n - rank(A); to intersect two affine subspaces, intersect their direction subspaces and check the offset difference lies in the sum of the directions for nonemptiness.

title: Column/row space reasoning for Ax=b and matrix products
trigger: Ax=b is solvable iff b lies in Col(A) (rank(A)=rank([A|b])); for a product AB, Col(AB) is contained in Col(A) and Row(AB) is contained in Row(B), so use these inclusions to judge which statements about rank/solvability/subspace containment hold.

title: Similarity vs equivalence of two matrices representing the same map
trigger: If A and B are matrices of the same linear operator T in two different bases (domain=codomain), they are similar (B=P^{-1}AP) and share rank, determinant, trace, eigenvalues; if only row/column operations relate them (B=PAQ, or T maps between differing bases in different spaces) they are merely equivalent and only rank is guaranteed to match.

title: Tracking rank, nullity, or determinant through a similarity/equivalence chain
trigger: Given a chain like A~B (similar) and B equivalent to C, remember similarity preserves rank, nullity, determinant and eigenvalues, while equivalence preserves only rank; walk the chain link by link, carrying forward only the invariants each relation guarantees.

title: Verifying the inner product axioms for a candidate form
trigger: Check the candidate bilinear form against each inner product axiom in turn - symmetry <x,y>=<y,x>, bilinearity/linearity in each argument, and positive-definiteness <x,x> is greater than or equal to 0 with equality only at x=0 - a single failing axiom (often positive-definiteness when a minus sign is present) rules it out.

title: Fourier coefficients in an orthogonal basis
trigger: Given an orthogonal (not necessarily orthonormal) basis {v1,v2,v3}, write v = a*v1+b*v2+c*v3 by computing each coefficient as <v,vi>/<vi,vi> (dot product with vi over vi's squared norm) — no system-solving needed since cross terms vanish by orthogonality.

title: Dimension of orthogonal complement via n - dim(W)
trigger: For W defined by k independent linear equations (or spanned by k independent vectors) in R^n, dim(W-perp) = n - rank(W); if W is given by a spanning set, first row-reduce to find its rank, then subtract from n, and to find an actual vector in W-perp solve the orthogonality equations <x,wi>=0 for each spanning vector wi.

title: Foot of perpendicular / projection onto a line
trigger: To project point/vector v onto a line through the origin with direction d, compute proj = (v.d / d.d) * d; if the line doesn't pass through the origin, translate first, project the offset, then translate back.

title: Projection onto a plane via normal vector formula
trigger: For a plane W: ax+by+cz=0 with normal n=(a,b,c), the projection of v onto W is P_W(v) = v - (v.n / n.n) * n; recognize this whenever W is given as a single homogeneous linear equation in R^3 (a codimension-1 subspace) rather than as spanning vectors.

title: Constructing / verifying an orthonormal basis via Gram-Schmidt
trigger: Apply Gram-Schmidt to the given spanning set: u1=v1, u2=v2-(v2.u1/u1.u1)u1, ...; then normalize each ui by dividing by its norm; check any proposed 'orthonormal basis' answer by verifying pairwise dot products are 0 and each vector has unit norm.

title: Projection onto a span of 2+ vectors (subspace, not a plane equation)
trigger: When W is given as span{w1,w2,...} (not a single normal equation), first Gram-Schmidt the wi into an orthogonal basis u1,u2,..., then project v as the sum of (v.ui/ui.ui)*ui over that basis; for 'minimum distance to W', compute |v - proj_W(v)|.

title: Projection map as a linear operator: kernel, range, idempotence
trigger: Treat P_W as a linear map on the ambient space: its range is W (dim = dim W), its kernel/nullspace is W-perp (dim = n - dim W), it fixes every vector already in W (P_W(w)=w), and it satisfies P_W^2 = P_W (idempotent) — use these facts directly instead of recomputing a formula for each true/false or dimension-count statement.

title: Orthogonal matrix identities: A^T A = I, unit rows/columns, det = ±1
trigger: A matrix A is orthogonal iff A^T A = I, equivalently its rows (and columns) are unit vectors that are pairwise orthogonal; from this derive det(A) = ±1, det(kA) = k^n det(A), row/column squared-norm sums equal 1, and count/construct matrices by imposing these row/column conditions directly on unknown entries.

title: Rotation matrices preserve norm and apply the standard rotation formula
trigger: A rotation about a coordinate axis by angle theta is an orthogonal transformation, so it leaves the length of any vector unchanged (|Rv|=|v|); to find the actual image, apply the standard 2D rotation matrix [[cos, -sin],[sin, cos]] to the two axes being rotated and leave the third coordinate fixed.

title: Mixed / one-off
trigger: Grab-bag true/false statement spanning independence, adjugate, similarity, and orthogonal sets simultaneously — evaluate each statement independently against its own definition rather than looking for one unifying technique.

title: Largest domain of a multivariable function
trigger: Identify what makes the formula undefined (denominator=0, negative under a root, log of non-positive) and exclude that set from R^2; the excluded set's shape (circle, disc, line) names the domain/boundary.

title: Range of a function via radial substitution
trigger: Rewrite in terms of r^2=x^2+y^2 (or the natural radial variable), let r range over the region's radii, and track the resulting single-variable function's output interval; check injectivity/surjectivity the same way.

title: Path-dependent limit: test multiple paths for disagreement
trigger: Plug in y=mx (or y=x^2, x=y^2, etc.) and see if the limit value depends on the path/parameter — if it does, the two-variable limit does not exist even though the function may still have well-defined partial derivatives at that point.

title: Algebraic limit evaluation and continuity patching
trigger: Simplify the expression algebraically (factor, rationalize, cancel) until direct substitution works; a required 'find k/c' or 'find missing value' question is just this simplified limit set equal to the value needed for continuity.

title: Squeeze / known single-variable limit substitution
trigger: Recognize a bounded factor times a vanishing factor (squeeze -> limit 0), or an expression of the form sin(u)/u with u->0 (limit 1 by the standard single-variable fact) even though u is a function of two variables.

title: Partial/directional derivatives at origin via limit definition
trigger: For a piecewise function defined separately at a point, don't use derivative rules there — go back to the limit definition f_x(0,0)=lim_{h->0}[f(h,0)-f(0,0)]/h (and similarly along any unit direction) to check existence.

title: Sign of partial derivatives at a point
trigger: Compute f_x and f_y as ordinary single-variable derivatives (treating the other variable as constant), evaluate at the given point, and read off the sign to decide increasing/decreasing behavior.

title: Directional derivative via gradient dot unit vector
trigger: Compute grad f at the point, normalize the given direction vector to unit length, and take the dot product D_u f = grad f . u — this single formula answers directional derivative, gradient-component, and 'solve for unknown parameter' variants alike.

title: Zero directional derivative: direction perpendicular to gradient
trigger: 'No change in direction u' means grad f . u = 0; set the dot product to zero and solve for the unknown component(s), using |u|=1 as a second equation when needed.

title: Comprehensive gradient/directional-derivative true-false statements
trigger: Check each claim against core facts: max directional derivative = |grad f| in the gradient's own direction, directional derivative in the zero-gradient case is 0 in every direction, mixed partials are equal when C^1/C^2, and critical points are where grad f=0 — verify statement-by-statement rather than computing one thing.

title: Level sets: shape and injectivity
trigger: Set f(x,y)=z0 and solve for the resulting curve (line, circle, etc.) to describe the level set; f is injective iff every level set is a single point.

title: Mixed / one-off
trigger: A sequence in R^n converges iff each coordinate sequence converges separately — check componentwise.

title: Critical point theory: definitions and horizontal-tangent-plane link
trigger: Recall that grad f(a,b)=0 at (a,b) IFF the tangent plane at that point is horizontal (parallel to the xy-plane, i.e. z=const); use this equivalence (and the definition/classification vocabulary: saddle, local max/min, degenerate) to answer conceptual/true-false items without computing anything.

title: Counting critical points by solving grad f = 0
trigger: Set f_x=0 and f_y=0, solve the resulting simultaneous polynomial equations (often factoring each variable's equation separately or by substitution), then count the number of real (x,y) solution pairs; for a 'largest region with a unique critical point' variant, first find all critical points this way, then take the minimum distance from the base point to the other critical points as the radius bound.

title: Steepest ascent/descent direction via normalized gradient
trigger: Compute grad f at the given point; the unit direction of steepest increase is grad f/|grad f|, steepest decrease is -grad f/|grad f|, and any direction orthogonal to grad f (rotate by 90 degrees, i.e. swap components and negate one) gives zero directional derivative — then extract the requested combination of components.

title: Linear (tangent-plane) approximation L(x,y) of a function
trigger: Build L(x,y) = f(a,b) + f_x(a,b)(x-a) + f_y(a,b)(y-b) at the given base point, then plug in the target point and match coefficients of any transcendental terms (e, etc.) to extract the requested constants.

title: Tangent line to a graph in a given direction (parametric point test)
trigger: The tangent line to z=f(x,y) at (a,b) in direction u=(u1,u2) is the parametrized set (a+t*u1, b+t*u2, f(a,b)+t*Df(a,b)*u); to test if a point lies on it, or to find missing coordinates/derivatives, solve for t from one coordinate and substitute into the others (this also lets you back out a directional derivative if only tangent-line data is given).

title: Tangent plane equation and point-membership checks
trigger: Write the tangent plane as z = f(a,b) + f_x(a,b)(x-a) + f_y(a,b)(y-b), rearrange to Ax+By+C=z, then either read off coefficients or substitute candidate points to check membership; for multi-surface matching problems, compute each surface's plane separately and compare against the given options; for 'consequences of tangent plane existence' items, recall it implies continuity and both partial derivatives exist at that point.

title: Tangent plane as affine subspace T = v + U: finding v and a basis for U
trigger: Recognize the tangent plane written as T(a,b) = v + U where U = span of directions with zero component along the normal (i.e. the plane through the origin parallel to the tangent plane) and v is any single point on the actual tangent plane; find v by evaluating f at the base point (giving the point (a,b,f(a,b))), and find a basis for U from two independent tangent directions, e.g. (1,0,f_x) and (0,1,f_y).

title: Minimizing distance from the origin to a plane (constrained optimization)
trigger: To minimize distance-squared from the origin to a constraint surface (e.g. a plane), substitute the constraint to reduce to two free variables, set both partials of the squared-distance function to zero, solve, and recover the requested linear combination of the point's coordinates.

title: Limit of tangent plane normal vectors along a point sequence
trigger: Express the tangent plane's normal vector (-f_x, -f_y, 1) at a moving point A_n, then take the limit of each component as n approaches the limiting point/infinity; for angle-with-an-axis questions, use cos(theta) = (normal . axis vector)/|normal| and take the limit of that expression.

title: Mixed / one-off
trigger: No shared technique with the rest of the week's set — for f(a,b)=det[[a,b],[b,a]], directly check the specific algebraic property asked (symmetry of the matrix, whether A^2=A, or the rank at the point) from the matrix definition.

title: Hessian test at a single given critical point
trigger: Find the critical point (f_x=0, f_y=0) if not given, then compute D = f_xx*f_yy - (f_xy)^2 there: D>0 & f_xx>0 => local min, D>0 & f_xx<0 => local max, D<0 => saddle, D=0 => test inconclusive.

title: Find and classify ALL critical points of f(x,y), then tally types
trigger: Solve f_x=0 and f_y=0 simultaneously to list every critical point of f, classify each with D=f_xx*f_yy-(f_xy)^2, then count how many fall in each category (max/min/saddle/indeterminate); if asked to evaluate f at a chosen extremum, plug that (x,y) back into f after classifying.

title: Classify a list of already-given candidate points
trigger: For each candidate point supplied in the list, directly substitute into f_xx, f_yy, f_xy to get D at that point and classify it — no need to search for critical points yourself, only check which listed points are genuinely critical and their type.

title: Hessian test with a parameter / rank-nullity degeneracy
trigger: Treat the parameter (e.g. k) as unknown inside D=f_xx*f_yy-(f_xy)^2; solve the inequality D(k)>0, <0, =0 to split into ranges giving max/min/saddle/inconclusive, and note that D=0 (or rank<2) means the Hessian is singular — nullity of the Hessian matrix signals the degenerate directions.

title: Constrained optimization by eliminating a variable (or AM-GM)
trigger: Use the linear constraint to solve for one variable and substitute it into the objective, reducing to an unconstrained function of the remaining variables; set its partial derivatives to zero to find the optimum (or, for a fixed-product/fixed-sum symmetric objective, apply AM-GM directly for the extreme value).

title: Piecewise function at a special point: continuity, partials, differentiability from definition
trigger: At the special point (origin, or a line like x=y where the piecewise formula is defined separately), compute f_x and f_y directly from the limit definition rather than differentiating the formula, then separately test whether those partials are continuous there and whether f itself is differentiable via the linear-approximation (epsilon) definition.

title: Theory recognition: implications between continuity, differentiability, partial/directional derivatives
trigger: Match the question to the correct standard implication chain — differentiable at a point implies continuous there and implies all directional derivatives exist (equal to grad f . direction); continuous partial derivatives near a point imply f is differentiable there — pick the statement consistent with the right direction of implication, not its converse.

title: Hessian determinant for radial functions g(x^2+y^2)
trigger: For f=g(x^2+y^2), critical points occur on circles r^2=x^2+y^2=c where g'(c)=0; at each such c, the Hessian determinant reduces to an expression purely in c (via chain rule on g and g'), so solve g'(c)=0 first and then evaluate/minimize D(c) over those roots.

title: Distance-squared function optimization on a disc
trigger: To optimize distance from a point to a surface/curve, replace the distance by its square phi = x^2 + y^2 + f(x,y)^2 to avoid square roots, then solve grad(phi)=0 for interior critical points and compare with boundary values (r=R) to find global extrema.

title: Radial substitution r^2=x^2+y^2 for symmetric functions
trigger: When f depends only on x^2+y^2 (e.g. sin(x^2+y^2)), substitute r^2=x^2+y^2 to reduce to a single-variable function g(r), then find its extrema over the r-interval set by the region (interior disk, boundary circle, or all of R^2).

title: Second-derivative discriminant test to classify critical points
trigger: Find interior critical points via grad(f)=0, classify each with D=fxx*fyy-(fxy)^2 (D>0,fxx>0 -> local min; D>0,fxx<0 -> local max; D<0 -> saddle), then compare with boundary values to identify the absolute max/min on the closed disc.

title: Boundary restriction to single-variable functions
trigger: To analyze a function on part of a region's boundary, substitute the boundary curve's equation (e.g. y=-x^2+1 or y=0) into f(x,y) to get a single-variable function f(x); its critical points come from f'(x)=0, and these plus corner/endpoint values are the boundary candidates for absolute extrema.

title: Absolute extrema on a closed rectangle via four edges
trigger: On a rectangle [a,b]x[c,d], find interior critical points via grad(f)=0, then optimize f along each of the 4 fixed-boundary edges (hold x or y constant) as single-variable problems, plus evaluate the 4 corners; the global max/min is the largest/smallest of all these candidate values.

title: Absolute extrema on a closed triangular region
trigger: On a triangular region bounded by linear inequalities, find interior critical points via grad(f)=0, restrict f to each of the 3 edges as single-variable functions to find edge critical points, evaluate the 3 vertices, and compare all candidate values for the global extremum.
